properties.description: The dependency check works without tomllib, and says what it cannot read (tools/reflow2_check.py, 2026-08-06, 3 cases). HONEST ABOUT ITS LIMITS: on a synthetic manifest holding a multi-line inline table and a [dependencies.X] sub-table, it read the one shape it understands and NAMED BOTH it did not — \"'spans' spans lines, not read\" and \"[dependencies.subtable] sub-table form not read\" — rather than returning a short list that would read as a complete one. No `tomli`, no pip: the kit installs into other people's projects and a runtime dependency is a cost they did not agree to.
properties.findings: EQUIVALENCE: with tomllib blocked, the line reader returns results BYTE-IDENTICAL to tomllib on reflow2's own three Cargo manifests — same source, same v0.12.0 pin, the same five grouped crates. WHY IT EXISTS: the check shipped reading only tomllib and its first CI run on reflow2's own repo reported \"could not read any build file to check them\", because ubuntu-22.04 carries Python 3.10. Correct locally, inert on most CI in the world.
properties.name: The dependency check works without tomllib, and says what it cannot read
